column3: “Farmer” renders the one sowing; “seed” supplies the referent of “some.”
“Rocky ground” renders rock; “the seedlings” supplies a plural subject.
“The seedlings” supplies the object, which is singular in the Greek.
“I speak” supplies the verb and subject in the clause about the others.
“The seeds” supplies the subject; the Greek describes those who have heard, rather than those who hear.
“The seeds” supplies the subject; “the word” is supplied in the hearing clause.
“Their fruit” supplies the subject of not maturing.
“Jesus” supplies the possessive referent; “to see Him” is supplied.
The speech is placed before entering the boat; the Greek places the boarding first.
“The boat” supplies the subject of being swamped; “great” is added to the danger.
“Across the lake” makes the location more explicit.
“Jesus” supplies the subject; the Greek says he had put on no garment for a long time.
“The man” supplies the subject; the idiom “what to me and to you” becomes “What do You want with me.”
“Jesus” supplies the subject; “solitary places” renders deserts.
